subject: maths
title: Year 5 Division: Short Division and Remainders
seo_title: Year 5 Division Worksheets: Short Division, Remainders and Word Problems (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Solve problems involving division, choosing efficient strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret any remainder according to the context and express results as a whole number, decimal or fraction
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on division, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M5N07): short division (the bus stop method) of 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers, zeros in the quotient, remainders as fractions and decimals, rounding up or down in context, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Divide one digit at a time from the left. Then decide what the remainder means.
key_sub: 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1 = 4 1/4 = 4.25 (not 4.1). Round up when everyone needs a place, round down for full groups, and share the remainder when the thing can be split.
body_html:
The big idea

Division shares a number into equal groups. Short division works one digit at a time, from the left. Write the number under the “bus stop” and the divisor outside. Divide each digit. If there is a remainder, carry it: write it as a small digit in front of the next digit. The answer is called the quotient.

Worked examples

Check with the inverse

957 ÷ 4 = 239 r 1. Is it right?

Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 239 × 4 = 956 and 956 + 1 = 957.

Answer: Yes, it is right

Three ways to write a remainder

17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1. The 1 left over is 1 out of 4, so it is 14. As a decimal, 14 = 0.25.

Write it asHow17 ÷ 4
a whole number remainderWrite r and what is left4 r 1
a fractionRemainder over the divisor4 14
a decimalChange the fraction to a decimal4.25 (not 4.1)

Remainders in context: what does the question want?

The question asksDo this61 students, 8 in each minibus: 61 ÷ 8 = 7 r 5
How many are needed for everyone?Round up8 minibuses
How many full groups?Round down7 full minibuses
How many are left over?The remainder is the answer5 students

When the thing can be split, such as a pizza, a length or money, share the remainder too: 23 pizzas ÷ 4 = 5 r 3 = 5 34 pizzas each, and $45 ÷ 4 = $11.25 each.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing a zero (4028 ÷ 4 = 107)When the divisor does not go into a digit, write 0 in the quotient: 1007
A remainder bigger than the divisor (238 r 5 for ÷ 4)The divisor goes in once more: 239 r 1
Writing r 1 as .1 (17 ÷ 4 = 4.1)r 1 means 1 out of 4: 14 = 0.25, so 4.25
Rounding the wrong way (7 minibuses for 61 students)Ask: does everyone need a place? Then round up

faq.q: What division do Year 5 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 5 students solve division problems with efficient strategies such as short division, and interpret any remainder to suit the context, writing the result as a whole number, a decimal or a fraction (AC9M5N07).

faq.q: What is the bus stop method of division?
faq.a: It is the everyday name for short division. The number goes under a line shaped like a bus stop, the divisor sits outside, and you divide one digit at a time, carrying any remainder to the next digit.

faq.q: How do you write a remainder as a fraction or a decimal?
faq.a: Put the remainder over the divisor: 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1 = 4 1/4. Then change the fraction to a decimal: 1/4 = 0.25, so 17 ÷ 4 = 4.25, not 4.1.

faq.q: Is division on the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: NAPLAN numeracy is based on the Australian Curriculum, so Year 5 students can meet division and remainder word problems in March. Practising when to round up or down helps with these questions.

items.q: Use short division to work out 576 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 144. Check: 144 × 4 = 576.

items.q: William uses short division for 722 ÷ 6. First, 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1. What does he divide next?
items.e: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 2, so you divide 12 next: 12 ÷ 6 = 2. The whole answer: 120 r 2.

items.q: 522 ÷ 6 = 87. Which number sentence checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 87 × 6 = 522, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 8 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 8 = 1 r 6, carry the 6 to make 64; 64 ÷ 8 = 8. Answer: 118. Check: 118 × 8 = 944.

items.q: Use short division to work out 992 ÷ 4.
items.e: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 4 = 4 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Answer: 248. Check: 248 × 4 = 992.

items.q: Isla uses short division for 967 ÷ 4. First, 9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1. What does she divide next?
items.e: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 6, so you divide 16 next: 16 ÷ 4 = 4. The whole answer: 241 r 3.

items.q: Use short division to work out 446 ÷ 3.
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 3 = 4 r 2, carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 3 = 8 r 2. Answer: 148 r 2. Check: 148 × 3 + 2 = 446.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 6 = 5 r 2, carry the 2 to make 29; 29 ÷ 6 = 4 r 5. Answer: 154 r 5. Check: 154 × 6 + 5 = 929.

items.q: Matilda uses short division for 545 ÷ 3. First, 5 ÷ 3 = 1 r 2. What does she divide next?
items.e: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 r 2. The remainder 2 is 2 hundreds, which is 20 tens. Write it as a small 2 in front of the 4, so you divide 24 next: 24 ÷ 3 = 8. The whole answer: 181 r 2.

items.q: Use short division to work out 52 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Answer: 13. Check: 13 × 4 = 52.

items.q: Cooper works out 792 ÷ 6 = 110 r 2. What mistake did he make?
c: He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the quotient
He divided by the wrong number
items.e: Cooper divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 6 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 6 = 2. Answer: 132. Check: 132 × 6 = 792.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Answer: 15. Check: 15 × 3 = 45.

items.q: Use short division to work out 455 ÷ 7.
items.e: 7 does not go into 4, so carry the 4 to make 45; 45 ÷ 7 = 6 r 3, carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 7 = 5. Answer: 65. Check: 65 × 7 = 455.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 does not go into 4, so carry the 4 to make 47; 47 ÷ 8 = 5 r 7, carry the 7 to make 71; 71 ÷ 8 = 8 r 7. Answer: 58 r 7. Check: 58 × 8 + 7 = 471.

items.q: Use short division to work out 59 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 4 = 4 r 3. Answer: 14 r 3. Check: 14 × 4 + 3 = 59.

items.q: 616 ÷ 4 = 154. Which number sentence checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 154 × 4 = 616, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7; 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Answer: 72. Check: 72 × 4 = 288.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Answer: 18. Check: 18 × 3 = 54.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 6 = 5 r 2. Answer: 15 r 2. Check: 15 × 6 + 2 = 92.

items.q: Ava works out 696 ÷ 4 = 121 r 2. What mistake did she make?
c: She missed a 0 in the quotient
She did not carry the remainders
She divided by the wrong number
items.e: Ava divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 6 ÷ 4 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 29; 29 ÷ 4 = 7 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 174. Check: 174 × 4 = 696.

sets.title: 4-digit numbers ÷ 1-digit numbers, with zeros in the quotient

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 4891 ÷ 7?
items.e: 4891 is close to 4900, and 49 ÷ 7 = 7, so 4900 ÷ 7 = 700. The exact answer is 698 r 5.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 7 = 5; 7 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 7 = 3. Answer: 503. Check: 503 × 7 = 3521.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 4189 ÷ 6?
items.e: 4189 is close to 4200, and 42 ÷ 6 = 7, so 4200 ÷ 6 = 700. The exact answer is 698 r 1.

items.q: Use short division to work out 4425 ÷ 3.
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 3 = 4 r 2, carry the 2 to make 22; 22 ÷ 3 = 7 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Answer: 1475. Check: 1475 × 3 = 4425.

items.q: Grace works out 4012 ÷ 4 = 13. What mistake did she make?
c: She did not carry the remainders
She missed a 0 in the quotient
items.e: Check: 13 × 4 = 52, not 4012. When 4 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the quotient. 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the quotient; 4 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Answer: 1003. Check: 1003 × 4 = 4012.

items.q: Aarav works out 8808 ÷ 8 = 111. What mistake did he make?
c: He missed a 0 in the quotient
He did not carry the remainders
items.e: Check: 111 × 8 = 888, not 8808. When 8 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the quotient. 8 ÷ 8 = 1; 8 ÷ 8 = 1; 8 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the quotient; 8 ÷ 8 = 1. Answer: 1101. Check: 1101 × 8 = 8808.

items.q: Use short division to work out 6412 ÷ 6.
items.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1; 6 does not go into 4, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 4 to make 41; 41 ÷ 6 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 52; 52 ÷ 6 = 8 r 4. Answer: 1068 r 4. Check: 1068 × 6 + 4 = 6412.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 6 = 5 r 4, carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 6 = 7 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 6 = 2. Answer: 572. Check: 572 × 6 = 3432.

items.q: Use short division to work out 4032 ÷ 4.
items.e: 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the quotient; 4 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Answer: 1008. Check: 1008 × 4 = 4032.

items.q: Use short division to work out 2133 ÷ 9.
items.e: 9 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 9 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 9 = 3 r 6, carry the 6 to make 63; 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Answer: 237. Check: 237 × 9 = 2133.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5; 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Answer: 1516. Check: 1516 × 3 = 4548.

items.q: Use short division to work out 3903 ÷ 3.
items.e: 3 ÷ 3 = 1; 9 ÷ 3 = 3; 3 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the quotient; 3 ÷ 3 = 1. Answer: 1301. Check: 1301 × 3 = 3903.

items.q: Use short division to work out 3008 ÷ 4.
items.e: 4 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 30; 30 ÷ 4 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 4 = 5; 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Answer: 752. Check: 752 × 4 = 3008.

items.q: How many digits will the quotient of 5555 ÷ 3 have (not counting the remainder)?
items.e: 5 is at least 3, so the quotient starts in the thousands place. 5555 ÷ 3 = 1851 r 2.

items.q: Use short division to work out 4816 ÷ 5.
items.e: 5 does not go into 4, so carry the 4 to make 48; 48 ÷ 5 = 9 r 3, carry the 3 to make 31; 31 ÷ 5 = 6 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 5 = 3 r 1. Answer: 963 r 1. Check: 963 × 5 + 1 = 4816.

items.q: Charlotte works out 3515 ÷ 5 = 73. What mistake did she make?
c: She did not carry the remainders
She missed a 0 in the quotient
items.e: Check: 73 × 5 = 365, not 3515. When 5 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the quotient. 5 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 5 = 7; 5 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Answer: 703. Check: 703 × 5 = 3515.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 38; 38 ÷ 4 = 9 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7; 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Answer: 1971. Check: 1971 × 4 = 7884.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 8 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 8 = 4 r 3, carry the 3 to make 31; 31 ÷ 8 = 3 r 7. Answer: 343 r 7. Check: 343 × 8 + 7 = 2751.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1; 6 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 6 = 6; 6 ÷ 6 = 1. Answer: 1061. Check: 1061 × 6 = 6366.

items.q: How many digits will the quotient of 5809 ÷ 6 have (not counting the remainder)?
items.e: 5 is less than 6, so there are no thousands. The quotient starts in the hundreds place. 5809 ÷ 6 = 968 r 1.

sets.title: Remainders as whole numbers, fractions and decimals

items.q: 71 ÷ 4 = 17 r 3 = 17 34. Which decimal is the same?
items.e: 34 = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75, so 17 34 = 17.75. The remainder 3 is not 0.3: it is 3 out of 4.

items.q: Kai works out 99 ÷ 2 = 49 r 1 and writes the answer as 49.1. What is the correct decimal answer?
items.e: r 1 does not mean 0.1. It means 1 out of 2, so it is 12 = 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5. The answer is 49.5.

items.q: Work out 77 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 77 ÷ 4 = 19 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 4, so it is 14. Answer: 19 14.

items.q: Work out 89 ÷ 2. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 89 ÷ 2 = 44 r 1. The remainder 1 out of 2 is 12 = 0.5. So the answer is 44.5, not 44.1.

items.q: What is the remainder when 438 is divided by 9?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. 9 does not go into 4, so carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 9 = 4 r 7, carry the 7 to make 78; 78 ÷ 9 = 8 r 6. Answer: 48 r 6. Check: 48 × 9 + 6 = 438.

items.q: Ethan works out 629 ÷ 4 = 156 r 5. What mistake did he make?
c: He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the quotient
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 5 is more than 4, so 4 goes in once more: 5 − 4 = 1. The answer is 157 r 1. Check: 157 × 4 + 1 = 629.

items.q: Sienna works out 69 ÷ 4 = 17 r 1 and writes the answer as 17.1. What is the correct decimal answer?
items.e: r 1 does not mean 0.1. It means 1 out of 4, so it is 14 = 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25. The answer is 17.25.

items.q: 28 ÷ 5 = 5 r 3 = 5 35. Which decimal is the same?
items.e: 35 = 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6, so 5 35 = 5.6. The remainder 3 is not 0.3: it is 3 out of 5.

items.q: Work out 35 ÷ 8. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 35 ÷ 8 = 4 r 3. The remainder 3 is 3 out of 8, so it is 38. Answer: 4 38.

items.q: Work out 331 ÷ 9. Give the remainder as a whole number.
items.e: 9 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 9 = 3 r 6, carry the 6 to make 61; 61 ÷ 9 = 6 r 7. Answer: 36 r 7. Check: 36 × 9 + 7 = 331.

items.q: Work out 87 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 87 ÷ 5 = 17 r 2. The remainder 2 out of 5 is 25 = 0.4. So the answer is 17.4, not 17.2.

items.q: Work out 88 ÷ 7. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 88 ÷ 7 = 12 r 4. The remainder 4 is 4 out of 7, so it is 47. Answer: 12 47.

items.q: Work out 94 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 94 ÷ 4 = 23 r 2. The remainder 2 out of 4 is 24 = 0.5. So the answer is 23.5, not 23.2.

items.q: Work out 66 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a mixed numeral in its simplest form.
items.e: 66 ÷ 4 = 16 r 2. The remainder 2 out of 4 is 24. Simplify: divide the numerator and the denominator by 2 to get 12. Answer: 16 12.

items.q: Work out 61 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 61 ÷ 5 = 12 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 5, so it is 15. Answer: 12 15.

items.q: Work out 854 ÷ 9. Give the remainder as a whole number.
items.e: 9 does not go into 8, so carry the 8 to make 85; 85 ÷ 9 = 9 r 4, carry the 4 to make 44; 44 ÷ 9 = 4 r 8. Answer: 94 r 8. Check: 94 × 9 + 8 = 854.

items.q: Work out 53 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 53 ÷ 5 = 10 r 3. The remainder 3 out of 5 is 35 = 0.6. So the answer is 10.6, not 10.3.

items.q: Work out 63 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 63 ÷ 4 = 15 r 3. The remainder 3 out of 4 is 34 = 0.75. So the answer is 15.75, not 15.3.

items.q: Work out 25 ÷ 3. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 25 ÷ 3 = 8 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 3, so it is 13. Answer: 8 13.

items.q: You divide a number by 6. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 6, the remainder can only be 1 to 5 (or 0). If you have 6 or more left, 6 goes in again.

sets.title: Interpret the remainder: round up, round down or share it

items.q: A shop has 139 batteries. It sells them in packs of 4. How many full packs can the shop make?
items.e: 139 ÷ 4 = 34 r 3. The 3 batteries left over are not enough to make another pack, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 34 packs.

items.q: A farm packs 44 eggs into cartons of 6. 44 ÷ 6 = 7 r 2. To find how many cartons are full, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: A carton with fewer than 6 eggs is not full, so ignore the remainder. Round down. The answer is 7 full cartons.

items.q: 224 students sign up for tug of war at the sports carnival. Each team needs exactly 9 students. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: 224 ÷ 9 = 24 r 8. The 8 students left over are not enough to make another team, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 24 teams.

items.q: A teacher shares 83 stickers equally between 6 groups. Each group gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: 83 ÷ 6 = 13 r 5. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 5 stickers.

items.q: 174 students are going on a school excursion. Each minibus has 9 seats for students. Jack works out 174 ÷ 9 = 19 r 3 and says 19 minibuses are needed. What is the right answer?
items.e: 19 minibuses only seat 19 × 9 = 171 students. The other 3 students still need seats, so Jack rounded the wrong way. Round up: 20 minibuses.

items.q: A 39 m rope is cut into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 39 ÷ 5 = 7 r 4. Rope can be cut into parts, so share the 4 m left over: 45 = 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8. Each piece is 7.8 m, not 7.4 m.

items.q: A coach puts 204 tennis balls into buckets of 9 and fills as many buckets as possible. How many balls are not in a bucket?
items.e: 204 ÷ 9 = 22 r 6. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 6 balls.

items.q: A farmer has 134 avocados. She packs them in bags of 4. How many full bags can she pack?
items.e: 134 ÷ 4 = 33 r 2. The 2 avocados left over are not enough to fill another bag, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 33 bags.

items.q: 149 guests are coming to the school trivia night. Each table seats 8 guests. How many tables are needed?
items.e: 149 ÷ 8 = 18 r 5. 18 tables hold 18 × 8 = 144 guests. 5 guests still need a place, so you need 1 more: 19 tables. Round up.

items.q: 247 Year 5 students are going on school camp. Each tent sleeps 4 students. How many tents are needed?
items.e: 247 ÷ 4 = 61 r 3. 61 tents hold 61 × 4 = 244 students. 3 students still need a place, so you need 1 more: 62 tents. Round up.

items.q: At the athletics carnival, 171 students line up in rows of 4 for the march past. How many students are in the last row, which is not full?
items.e: 171 ÷ 4 = 42 r 3. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 3 students.

items.q: A teacher needs 184 glue sticks for the term. Glue sticks come in packs of 6. How many packs must she buy?
items.e: 184 ÷ 6 = 30 r 4. 30 packs give 30 × 6 = 180 glue sticks. She still needs 4 glue sticks more, so she must buy 1 more pack: 31 packs. Round up.

items.q: 51 people are going to a footy match. Each car takes 4 people. 51 ÷ 4 = 12 r 3. To find how many cars are needed, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: Everyone needs a seat, so the left-over people need 1 more car. Round up. The answer is 13 cars.

items.q: The school library has 346 new books. Each shelf holds 9 books. How many shelves can be filled completely?
items.e: 346 ÷ 9 = 38 r 4. The 4 books left over are not enough to fill another shelf, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 38 shelves.

items.q: 17 cakes are shared equally between 3 classes for an end-of-term party. How much cake does each class get? Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 17 ÷ 3 = 5 r 2. The 2 left-over cakes can be cut and shared too: 2 ÷ 3 = 23. Each class gets 5 23 cakes.

items.q: 182 students are going on an excursion. Each parent’s car can take 3 students. How many cars are needed?
items.e: 182 ÷ 3 = 60 r 2. 60 cars hold 60 × 3 = 180 students. 2 students still need a place, so you need 1 more: 61 cars. Round up.

items.q: 3 friends share 23 pizzas equally. 23 ÷ 3 = 7 r 2. To find how much pizza each friend gets, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: Pizzas can be cut into equal parts, so the left-over pizzas are shared too. Write the remainder as a fraction. The answer is 7 23 pizzas.

items.q: A canteen has 146 muffins. It packs them in boxes of 6. Oliver works out 146 ÷ 6 = 24 r 2 and says 25 boxes can be filled. What is the right answer?
items.e: 25 boxes would need 25 × 6 = 150 muffins, but there are only 146. The 2 muffins left over cannot fill a box, so Oliver rounded the wrong way. Round down: 24 boxes.

items.q: 67 students are going to the swimming carnival. Each minibus has 8 seats for students. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: 67 ÷ 8 = 8 r 3. 8 minibuses hold 8 × 8 = 64 students. 3 students still need a place, so you need 1 more: 9 minibuses. Round up.

items.q: A bakery has 105 lamingtons. Each box holds 6 lamingtons. How many boxes can be filled?
items.e: 105 ÷ 6 = 17 r 3. The 3 lamingtons left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 17 boxes.

sets.title: Word problems: sharing money, sports teams and packing

items.q: A class raises $952 at a sausage sizzle. The money is shared equally between 4 charities. How much does each charity get?
items.e: Divide: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 4 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 4 = 8. So 952 ÷ 4 = 238. The answer is $238. Check: 238 × 4 = 952.

items.q: Amelia bakes 43 slices of banana bread. She shares them equally between 4 friends. How many slices does each friend get?
items.e: Divide: 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the quotient and the remainder is 3. So 43 ÷ 4 = 10 r 3. The 3 left over can be shared too: 3 ÷ 4 = 34. Each gets 10 34 slices.

items.q: A school spends $3186 on 9 new laptops. Each laptop costs the same. How much does one laptop cost?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 31; 31 ÷ 9 = 3 r 4, carry the 4 to make 48; 48 ÷ 9 = 5 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 9 = 4. So 3186 ÷ 9 = 354. The answer is $354. Check: 354 × 9 = 3186.

items.q: William and 4 friends have lunch at a café. They split the $57 bill equally. How much does each person pay?
items.e: Divide: 5 ÷ 5 = 1; 7 ÷ 5 = 1 r 2. So 57 ÷ 5 = 11 r 2. Dollars can be shared into cents, so share the $2 left over: $2 ÷ 5 = 40c. Each share is $11.40, not $11.20.

items.q: 232 students are going to the athletics carnival. Each minibus has 9 seats for students. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 9 = 2 r 5, carry the 5 to make 52; 52 ÷ 9 = 5 r 7. So 232 ÷ 9 = 25 r 7. 25 minibuses are not enough: 7 students would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 26 minibuses.

items.q: The class has $164 to spend on skipping ropes. Each skipping rope costs $9. How many skipping ropes can the class buy?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 9 = 1 r 7, carry the 7 to make 74; 74 ÷ 9 = 8 r 2. So 164 ÷ 9 = 18 r 2. The $2 left over is not enough to buy another skipping rope, so round down. The answer is 18 skipping ropes.

items.q: 4 friends win $988 in a school art competition. They share the prize equally. How much does each friend get?
items.e: Divide: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 4 = 4 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7. So 988 ÷ 4 = 247. The answer is $247. Check: 247 × 4 = 988.

items.q: A 74 m length of fencing is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Divide: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 4 = 8 r 2. So 74 ÷ 4 = 18 r 2. A length can be split into parts, so write the remainder as a decimal: 24 = 2 ÷ 4 = 0.5. Each piece is 18.5 m, not 18.2 m.

items.q: 188 people are coming to the school concert. The chairs are put out in rows of 8. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 8 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 8 = 3 r 4. So 188 ÷ 8 = 23 r 4. 23 rows are not enough: 4 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 24 rows.

items.q: A school orders 1254 exercise books. They come in packs of 6. How many packs does the school order?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 6 = 2; 6 does not go into 5, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 6 = 9. So 1254 ÷ 6 = 209. There is no remainder, so the answer is 209 packs. Check: 209 × 6 = 1254.

items.q: Liam deals 271 playing cards equally to 7 players. Each player gets as many as possible. How many cards are left over?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 7 = 3 r 6, carry the 6 to make 61; 61 ÷ 7 = 8 r 5. So 271 ÷ 7 = 38 r 5. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 5 cards.

items.q: A nursery has 1124 seedlings. It plants them in trays of 8 and fills as many trays as it can. How many seedlings are not in a tray?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 8 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 8 = 4; 8 does not go into 4, so write 0 in the quotient and the remainder is 4. So 1124 ÷ 8 = 140 r 4. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 4 seedlings.

items.q: 195 students sign up for netball. Each team needs exactly 7 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 7 = 2 r 5, carry the 5 to make 55; 55 ÷ 7 = 7 r 6. So 195 ÷ 7 = 27 r 6. The 6 students left over are not enough to make another team, so round down. The answer is 27 teams.

items.q: 206 students are at the athletics carnival. Each relay team needs exactly 4 runners. How many full relay teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 4 = 5; 6 ÷ 4 = 1 r 2. So 206 ÷ 4 = 51 r 2. The 2 students left over are not enough to make another team, so round down. The answer is 51 teams.

items.q: A farm collects 551 eggs. It packs them in cartons of 6. How many cartons does it need for all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 55; 55 ÷ 6 = 9 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 6 = 1 r 5. So 551 ÷ 6 = 91 r 5. 91 cartons are not enough: 5 eggs would still need a carton. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 92 cartons.

items.q: A farm packs 2091 mangoes into trays of 9. How many full trays can it pack?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 9 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 29; 29 ÷ 9 = 3 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 9 = 2 r 3. So 2091 ÷ 9 = 232 r 3. The 3 mangoes left over are not enough to fill another tray, so round down. The answer is 232 trays.

items.q: Cooper runs 2136 m by running 8 laps of the school oval. Each lap is the same length. How long is one lap?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 8 = 2 r 5, carry the 5 to make 53; 53 ÷ 8 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 56; 56 ÷ 8 = 7. So 2136 ÷ 8 = 267. There is no remainder, so the answer is 267 m. Check: 267 × 8 = 2136.

items.q: A book has 159 pages. Ava reads the same number of pages each day and finishes it in 3 days. How many pages does she read each day?
items.e: Divide: 3 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5; 9 ÷ 3 = 3. So 159 ÷ 3 = 53. There is no remainder, so the answer is 53 pages. Check: 53 × 3 = 159.

items.q: Lachlan is putting 218 photos into an album. Each page holds 4 photos. How many pages does he need?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 4 = 5 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 4 = 4 r 2. So 218 ÷ 4 = 54 r 2. 54 pages are not enough: 2 photos would still need a page. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 55 pages.

items.q: 4 friends earn $142 washing cars. They share the money equally. How much does each friend get?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 4 = 3 r 2, carry the 2 to make 22; 22 ÷ 4 = 5 r 2. So 142 ÷ 4 = 35 r 2. Dollars can be shared into cents, so share the $2 left over: $2 ÷ 4 = 50c. Each share is $35.50, not $35.20.
